title: 3.4.9 Plain English to Pseudocode: A Function That Calls Its Parameter Twice
description: Turn four plain-English steps into pseudocode for applyTwice: read the operation and the value, make the first call, make the second call on its result, and print.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Read in `operation` and `value`.

**2.** Call `operation` on `value`. Call the answer `first`.

**3.** Call `operation` again, this time on `first`. Call that answer `second`.

**4.** Print `second`.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor (open the Flow Chart bar). You do not draw it, you read it: it is a straight line, so there is no diamond and nothing loops back. Each box is one step.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Number every line, including indented ones. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `SET lives TO 3` (start a value)
- `IF lives is 0` ... `END IF` (a check, with the steps inside it indented)
- `FOR EACH life IN lives` ... `END FOR` (repeat for every item)
- `PRINT lives` (show something)

Plain English is fine here. Press **Grade** above the editor: the AI reads what your steps mean and marks each Quest card green or red. Changing your text clears its marks, so press Grade again when you have finished editing.

Before you submit, trace it by hand: `operation` is `(n) => n * 2` and `value` is `5`. The first call gives `10`, the second gives `20`, and `20` is what prints. If your steps print before the second call, they are wrong even if Grade is green.
hints: The second call uses the answer of the first call, not `value` again.
The print is the last step, after both calls.

requirements.title: Numbered steps
requirements.description: Number your steps 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: Write at least four lines that start with a number, each with a step written after it.

requirements.title: Reads operation and value
requirements.description: Read in both operation and value.
requirements.hint: Start by reading in both the operation and the value.

requirements.title: The first call
requirements.description: Call operation on value and keep the answer.
requirements.hint: Add a step that calls operation on value (name the answer first).

requirements.title: The second call uses the first answer
requirements.description: After the first call, call operation again on the first answer.
requirements.hint: After the first call, add a step that calls operation again on first (not on value).

requirements.title: It prints the second answer
requirements.description: Print the answer of the second call.
requirements.hint: Print the answer of the second call (second), not value or first.

requirements.title: The print comes last
requirements.description: The print is the last step, after both calls.
requirements.hint: Move the print to the end, after both calls.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your steps
aiCheck.prompt: The student was given four plain-English steps and rewrote them as numbered, step-by-step pseudocode in README.md, between a first line and a last line that were already there. The function is: function applyTwice(operation, value) { return operation(operation(value)); } called as applyTwice((n) => n * 2, 5). The point is that operation(operation(value)) is TWO calls with the inner one finishing first: read operation and value, call operation on value (first), call operation again on that answer (second), then print second. There is no decision and no loop. Judge each criterion ONLY by whether its idea is present in the student's steps, however they word it. Plain English, keywords such as SET, IF, ELSE, END IF, FOR EACH, END FOR, CALL, PRINT, or a mix of both are all fine, and so are different names, different capitalisation, and different ways to number the lines. Do not require any particular keyword. A step that is clearly aimed at the criterion is enough for 'met'. Mark a criterion 'missing' only when the idea is absent or the steps do the opposite (for example the second call using value again instead of the first answer). Write each note for THIS student's own steps: in a not-met note, name the exact step or word in their steps that causes the problem (quote at most a few words), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected steps. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their steps satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.

rubric.title: Numbered steps
rubric.description: The student numbered their steps (1. 2. 3. or similar), at least four of them.

rubric.title: Reads operation and value
rubric.description: The steps take in both operation and value.

rubric.title: The first call
rubric.description: A step calls operation on value and keeps the answer. A single step that nests both calls, such as operation(operation(value)), also counts for this one.

rubric.title: The second call uses the first answer
rubric.description: AFTER the first call, a step calls operation again on the first call's answer. Calling it again on value, or only calling it once, is missing.

rubric.title: It prints the second answer
rubric.description: The step that prints shows the answer of the SECOND call, not value or the first answer.

rubric.title: The print comes last
rubric.description: The print is the last step, after both calls. A print before the second call is missing.
